## Appendix A. Quality checklist

Use this checklist to self-review before running an evaluation or asking someone else to review its quality.

### Scenario quality

- [ ] The prompt is something a developer would actually type
- [ ] Contains no evaluation metadata, scoring hints, or instructions about how to be evaluated
- [ ] Be mindful of vocabulary: developers may not know the internal product names or specific terms your team uses. Don't assume they'll use the "right" words

### Criteria quality: accuracy

- [ ] You have a prerequisite gate: one or at most two unconditional checks. If they don't pass, further evaluation makes no sense. Example: you ask the agent to build a database solution assuming Cosmos DB (without naming it), and the agent writes MongoDB code. Evaluating the correctness of that MongoDB solution is pointless because the basic technology choice is wrong.
- [ ] Each criterion tests an aspect of your technology that matters for correct usage
- [ ] Pass conditions describe what correct usage looks like with specific packages, versions, or APIs named
- [ ] Fail conditions describe specific incorrect patterns (not just "does not use the technology correctly")
- [ ] Skip conditions cover cases where the criterion doesn't apply
- [ ] A perfect implementation would pass all criteria
- [ ] A clearly broken implementation would fail at least one criterion

### Criteria quality: calibration

- [ ] Criteria are aligned with reasonable expectations for a developer using this technology, not with what your extension provides
- [ ] No criterion is so loose that everything passes
- [ ] No criterion is so strict that only one exact implementation passes
- [ ] Each criterion tests one thing (not multiple concerns in one criterion)
- [ ] Criteria test correctness, not style
- [ ] Criteria don't test things the agent can't control

### Criteria quality: consistency

- [ ] Each criterion has explicit pass/fail/skip conditions that leave nothing to interpretation
- [ ] Criteria use technology-specific vocabulary the judge can verify (package names, API patterns, config keys) rather than vague quality terms

### Criteria calibration

- [ ] Each criterion passes a known-good artifact and fails a known-bad artifact
- [ ] Repeated judgments of the same artifacts produce consistent verdicts
- [ ] Someone who knows the product has confirmed technical accuracy
- [ ] Repeated scoring has confirmed the wording produces consistent verdicts
- [ ] Calibration runs are kept separate from production results

### Criteria maintenance

- [ ] The locked criteria set has a version, and production results record that version
- [ ] Material changes to the product, scenario, or starting workspace trigger a criteria review
- [ ] Criteria for older product versions are retained only while those versions remain supported
- [ ] Defects found after production are documented and corrected in a new criteria-set version
- [ ] Judge changes preserve backward compatibility or establish a clearly labeled measurement boundary

### Profile selection

- [ ] Bare baseline is included (unless you're only comparing extension variations)
- [ ] If there's an extension to compare, at least one extension profile is included
- [ ] If there's no extension yet, running just the baseline is fine. It tells you whether gaps exist and helps you decide how to address them.
- [ ] Each profile tests a specific question

### Before running

- [ ] At least 5 runs per scenario-profile combination
- [ ] Use environment and agent where the majority of your audience is to ensure you're optimizing for the maximum impact first

### Ongoing measurement

- [ ] Rerun cadence reflects changes to the coding agents your audience uses and the team's capacity to respond
- [ ] Recurring evaluations use the same locked definition so that results remain comparable
- [ ] Product, scenario, or criteria changes start a new version rather than continuing the old trend

### Evaluation system readiness

- [ ] Reproduces the operating system, harness, model, and extensions used by the largest audience cohort
- [ ] Configures scenarios, starting workspaces, criteria, and profiles independently
- [ ] Resets every run to the same starting workspace and runs each scenario-profile combination repeatedly
- [ ] Supports mechanical gates and structured checks for verifiable outcomes
- [ ] Supports context-aware criteria with explicit pass, fail, and skip conditions for semantic decisions
- [ ] Preserves generated artifacts, verdict evidence, execution results, task costs, and complete trajectories per run
- [ ] Compares extension profiles against a bare baseline, including quality and task cost
- [ ] Keeps run-level evidence available when results are aggregated
